items.title: NotebookLM: DIY Not EMI: 2026-04-26
items.description: Anarcho-punk is an ideological subgenre of punk rock that emerged in the late 1970s to passionately promote anarchism, animal rights, and the anti-war movement. The subculture champions a strict do-it-yourself ethic that consciously rejects major record labels in favor of underground cassette networks and self-published zines. Rather than focusing solely on musical delivery, these bands prioritize a totalized aesthetic where the political message dictates the creative process and the lifestyles of the members.
items.quote: Anarcho-punk bands are often less focused on particular musical delivery and more focused on a totalised aesthetic that encompasses the entire creative process, from album and concert art, to political message, and to the lifestyles of the band members.

items.title: NotebookLM: Blackgaze Dynamics 2026-04-25
items.description: Blackgaze is an experimental fusion genre that blends the abrasive intensity of black metal with the hazy, heavily distorted guitar textures of shoegaze. The style is heavily characterized by radical dynamic contrasts, shifting abruptly from quiet, reflective melodies into overwhelmingly loud walls of sound and aggressive blast-beat drumming. By pairing harsh shrieked vocals with dreamy atmospheres, the genre pushes extreme music into highly emotional and expansive new territories.
items.quote: melding its blast beats, dungeon wailing and razorwire guitars with the more reflective melodies of post-rock, shoegaze and post-hardcore.

items.title: NotebookLM: Deep South Sludge 2026-04-24
items.description: Sludge metal is an extreme subgenre of heavy metal born in the American Deep South that fuses the slow, trudging tempos of doom metal with the raw aggression of hardcore punk. The music is characterized by heavily distorted, down-tuned guitars, abrasive screamed vocals, and an intensely visceral atmosphere. Lyrically, the genre typically explores harsh, real-world themes such as poverty, addiction, and pollution with a sneering sense of nihilism.
items.quote: Eyehategod started as a way to piss people off... All the heavy music around here was fast, thrashy stuff, so Eyehategod slowed it down as much as possible and made a bunch of noise, basically.
items.quote_source: Mike Williams, quoted in 'Doomed to Fail: The Incredibly Loud History of Doom, Sludge, and Post-Metal' by J.J. Anselmi

items.title: NotebookLM: Zeuhl Celestial Forces 2026-04-12
items.description: Zeuhl is an experimental music genre blending jazz fusion, symphonic rock, and neoclassical elements that was pioneered in 1969 by the French band Magma. The style is heavily characterized by hypnotic, repetitive structures, pumping bass rhythms, and dramatic polyphonic choral movements. Often sung in the constructed language Kobaïan, the music is designed to evoke a visceral, spiritual, and celestial force.
items.quote: about what you'd expect an alien rock opera to sound like: massed, chanted choral motifs, martial, repetitive percussion, sudden bursts of explosive improv and just as unexpected lapses into eerie, minimalist trance-rock.
items.quote_source: Dominique Leone, writing for Pitchfork (cited in Zeuhl - Wikipedia)

items.title: NotebookLM: Math Rock Essentials 2026-04-10
items.description: Math rock is a style of alternative and indie rock characterized by complex, atypical rhythmic structures, odd time signatures, and extended chords. The genre typically features smaller ensembles that prioritize intricate guitar playing, often treating the voice as just another instrument in the mix rather than the focal point. While it shares similarities with post-rock, math rock generally opts for a more tightly wound and 'rockier' approach to songwriting.
items.quote: tinker with pop the way a born mathematician tinkers with numbers

It eschews the purely mechanical sounds of early industrial music in favor of more melodic riffs, harsh vocals, and atmospheric synthesizer arrangements. The genre leans heavily into futuristic aesthetics and creates an aggressive, dystopian soundscape.
